newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares retrench to end run of record highs.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares retrench to end run of record highs.

text.p: Danish share prices closed lower on Thursday ending a run of eight consecutive trading days with end-of-day all-time highs for the KFX index, with dealers seeing more declines ahead before the market rises again.
"The extent of the market retrenchment was much less than we feared. A period of falls will not be a bad thing, giving us a breather before the index climbs again," one dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index lost 0.20 point to close at 126.29 in overall bourse turnover of 1.944 billion crowns. The KFX December future rose 0.65 point to 126.40 with 10 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Novo Nordisk attracted a good deal of attention following its announcement of 400 million crown rationalisation cuts for 1997 and 1998, finishing the day a solid 21 crowns up at 954.
But this was not sufficient to drag the index out of the doldrums.

Banks slipped, with Den Danske closing four crowns lower at 425, Unidanmark shedding three crowns to 284, while BG Bank only lost a single crown to end at 242 and Jyske Bank remained unchanged at 418.
